review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the likely candidates. `timeLinear` is a named specialisation of `ContinuousLinearMap.prodMap` and `EnvelopeJets` is a bespoke predicate. I judged neither to be a clear Mathlib duplicate, so I did not report them. `normalizedMatrix` is a different case: it is pointwise scalar multiplication of `Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ`, which Mathlib already provides as `•`. It also has a custom determinant lemma and is reused in other files. I found a same-named but unrelated `normalizedMatrix` in PulseAmplitude. I did not use it as evidence. I did not run Lean, so the proposed replacement is untested.

findings.excerpt: SmoothCovariance.Mat2 := fun i j => r * H i j
findings.problem: `normalizedMatrix r H` is scalar multiplication of a `Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ` (`SmoothCovariance.Mat2` is an abbrev for it) written entrywise. Mathlib's `Matrix` already has the `•` action, and `(r • H) i j` unfolds to `r * H i j`. The file proves `normalizedMatrix_det` by hand with `Matrix.det_fin_two` and `ring`, which duplicates `Matrix.det_smul`. The custom definition also blocks the generic `smul` simp set, `smul_smul` and `Matrix.smul_apply`. Downstream files therefore reprove scaling facts. ActualSignedGeometry proves `normalizedMatrix R H = normalizedMatrix (R / r) (normalizedMatrix r H)` by `ext; simp only [normalizedMatrix]; field_simp`, which is just `smul_smul`. They also cite the custom `normalizedMatrix_det`.
findings.proposed_change: Make the concept `r • H`. Either replace `normalizedMatrix r H` by `r • H` throughout, or keep the name as `abbrev normalizedMatrix (r : ℝ) (H : SmoothCovariance.Mat2) : SmoothCovariance.Mat2 := r • H`. Derive `normalizedMatrix_det` from `Matrix.det_smul`, with `Fintype.card (Fin 2) = 2`. Then use `smul_smul` in the downstream composition lemma. The name and statements stay available to the other files, and the entrywise `r * H i j` forms can come from `Matrix.smul_apply` and `smul_eq_mul`.
findings.benefit: Readers get the standard Mathlib action instead of a parallel scaling operation. The determinant and composition lemmas come from Mathlib, so the per-file `ext`/`field_simp` proofs disappear. Normalised matrices then interoperate with other matrix lemmas without unfolding.
